findings.title: Default getThreads sends an all-null SLA filter that becomes invalid SQL
findings.failure: Every MCP getThreads call that leaves slaStatuses and slaTypes null (the default, including every existing caller) fails in Postgres with a syntax error. The operation always sends serviceLevelAgreements: { statuses: null, types: null }. ThreadsFilter keeps that as a non-null object and defaults the omitted updatedAt to null. The top-level filter builder then emits an empty SQL fragment, and slonik joins it with AND next to the createdAt clause, which is always present in this same query and becomes `1 = 1` when both bounds are null. The WHERE clause is `... AND ( AND 1 = 1)` (or `1 = 1 AND ` if key order differs). Postgres rejects that (SQLSTATE 42601). Calls that set slaStatuses or slaTypes still work, because those produce a non-empty EXISTS fragment. searchThreads and getThreadDetails are unaffected.
findings.fix: Do not inline the object. Pass one variable the way surveyResponse already does: `$serviceLevelAgreements: ServiceLevelAgreementFilter = null` and `serviceLevelAgreements: $serviceLevelAgreements`. buildFilters skips a null value. If the tool must keep two flat parameters, change the all-null branch in the top-level serviceLevelAgreements filter to `return sql.fragment`1 = 1`` (the surveyResponse all-null branch already does this). An empty fragment is only safe when the parent key is null.
findings.evidence: getThreads.graphql always builds the object and already always builds createdAt the same way (lines 93-96). threadsFilter.ts:58-73 parses a present object and defaults updatedAt to null instead of collapsing it. threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943-947 returns sql.fragment`` when statuses, types, and updatedAt are null; the nested path at lines 647-686 no-ops that case, but getThreads uses createFilters → buildBaseFilterSql → buildFilters, not that path. surveyResponse at threadDbFilterUtils.ts:1156-1164 returns `1=1` for an all-null object. packages/db/src/filtering.ts:14-31 rangeFilter returns ignoreFilter (`1 = 1`) when both bounds are null; buildFilters (lines 114-125) uses lodash compact, which drops only false, null, 0, "", undefined, and NaN, so a FragmentSqlToken stays, then sql.join glues the parts with ` AND `. threadDbFilterUtils.ts:1276-1278 wraps that in parentheses; threadDb.ts:1252 places it after AND in the WHERE clause. slonik 45.5.0 (pnpm-lock.yaml) serializes a SLONIK_TOKEN_LIST by concatenating each member's sql and inserting the glue between members, including a member whose sql is empty (gajus/slonik v45.5.0 src/factories/createSqlTokenSqlFragment.ts). apollo-mcp-server v1.20.0 (services/mcp-server/Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh) sends the operation file as the query document, so the inline object is not omitted when the variables default to null. GraphQL input coercion keeps an input object whose fields are null (GraphQL spec, Input Coercion); it does not turn that object into null.

findings.title: The SLA status selection is copied twelve times
findings.failure: Each of the four targets repeats the same six inline fragments, and that block is repeated in all three operations. Adding or renaming a status field in one copy leaves the others returning a thinner SLA payload. Each copy is still a valid selection on its own, so validation does not catch the drift.
findings.fix: In each operation file, define one named fragment on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail and spread it on firstResponseTime, nextResponseTime, firstResolutionTime, and totalResolutionTime. Match the per-operation fragment prefix already used by GetBroadcastsActor in services/mcp-server/operations/getBroadcasts.graphql. validateMcpOperations.ts concatenates every operation into one document, so the fragment name has to stay unique across files.
findings.evidence: Repo search for ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending hits only these three files, four times each. Named fragments in services/mcp-server/operations/*.graphql are the existing way this directory shares a selection set inside one operation.

checked_fine: Selection sets match the schema: ServiceLevelAgreementStatusSummary targets are nullable unions; Pending and ImminentBreach expose breachingAt (resolver maps breachTime), pausedAt, and remainingMinutesAtPause; Breaching exposes breachedAt; Achieved maps achievedAt from completedAt; Breached exposes breachedAt and completedAt; Cancelled exposes cancelledAt. DateTime.iso8601 exists. Model enums PENDING, IMMINENT_BREACH, BREACHING, BREACHED, ACHIEVED, CANCELLED and the four SLA types match the GraphQL enums.
Non-null timestamps on those union members are required by the tracker zod variants (breachTime, breachedAt, completedAt, cancelledAt), so requesting them does not introduce a new null-bubble.

serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary returns all-null without a tracker query when tierId and serviceLevelAgreementPolicyId are both null (resolvers.ts). Otherwise serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDataLoader batches getLatestServiceLevelAgreementTrackersByThreadIdsUnsafe. The threads query already requires thread:read; the public Thread type already exposes this field.
searchThreads and getThreadDetails only add the summary field. They do not send a serviceLevelAgreements object.

The tool comment is accurate: the filter is EXISTS over any service_level_agreement_trackers row, and the partial unique index idx_sla_tracker_unique_thread_id_service_level_agreement_id allows a completed or cancelled row beside a newer open tracker. The summary is the latest row per type.

Empty slaStatuses or slaTypes arrays fail Zod minLength(1), the same rule as labelTypeIds. Omitting the variable or passing null is what skips that dimension, once the object is no longer always sent.

No migration, export, env var, or permission change. Rollback is the MCP image (Dockerfile COPY operations/). The core API already had the field and the filter. Container health is GET /health, so a bad getThreads query does not fail the ECS health check.
Dead-code search for slaStatuses and slaTypes: the only production references are the new getThreads.graphql variables. The new selection sets are what the three MCP tools return.
